## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Glad to see Roomba getting a separate battery level entity. It removes the need for a sensor template. However, the new sensor entity has a static battery icon and doesn't show whether the Roomba is charging or not, while the icon in the Roomba entity itself shows this information. The new sensor entity should have an icon_template that reflects the Roomba entity.

review_comments: We don't add custom icon to sensor entities with device class set. That should be handled by the frontend.
That totally makes sense. But to achieve this, the frontend will need to know if the battery is charging. Maybe we need to add a property to sensor? This is gonna be an architecture issue.

We added a binary sensor device class for charging recently.

https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/issues/359

So with that entity the frontend should have the possibility to know if a device is charging or not, if the integration supports the device registry.

I'm not sure what the frontend status is.

The basic idea is to make a binary sensor with device class `battery_charging`.  I haven't finished the frontend work to make the frontend aware of these yet.  The old helper method you used here is currently the functional method and should no longer be needed once I do the frontend work.
